utterances.text: Thank you. Now, as a soldier, did you have shifts? Did you go to the front line and then home after that, after doing your shift?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We had to protect ourselves in the village. We didn't have a line. We just stood guard and watch over our village to prevent anybody from attacking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about during the time of operations? How long did your shifts last?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, a shift lasted about eight hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That means that there were three shifts in one day; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: During the shifts did the soldiers take their weapons home or did they stay up at the line?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. They would take them home and give them to the next man. I said we didn't have much weaponry. Now, after that, when they started taking our people away, arresting them, then all communication was interrupted. The Serbs were walking around. There was no war. The Serbs started rounding up people, and there was no communication later on, when people became more organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In the trial against President Milosevic, the Defence asked you what you used to kill that many Serbs with, and your answer was -- what was your answer?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: When that operation took place, they seized our -- or, rather, we seized weapons from your soldiers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I didn't object before, Your Honour, but your guidelines make clear that when citing a prior statement back to a witness, the party is to give the page and line, some indication of where this statement's from, and I would ask that the accused follow that guideline.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you bear that in mind, Mr. Karadzic. Do you need reference as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, we can continue. I just -- this is the second time, so in the future I would like references.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Agreed. Thank you. Continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I am looking for that now, because this question was out of my order of questions, whether they had weapons or not, but I will find the reference. I'm looking for it, for the statement and the particular reference. I'll give it to you later on. Anyway, I'd like to call up now 640, 1D00640. The next document, please. It's a Defence document, and we're going to tender it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, while we're waiting for that come up, let me ask you this: Mr. Nicholls said that your family was forced out by the Serbs from your village to Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Of course, because they would never have gone to Tuzla if the situation wasn't like that. First of all, you set fire to my house and all the food I had in my house, and the children couldn't eat earth. You can eat everything else, but not earth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. Now, may we turn to the second page of this document, please. But let's see what the heading is first. It says: "The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, report -- or, rather, Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, the Municipal Staff of the armed forces of Zvornik, report on the state, organisational, and formational structure and combat readiness of the units of the armed forces of Zvornik." It was drafted in Sapna on the 5th of November, 1992. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You don't agree?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. It wasn't drafted in Sapna. We had no communication with Sapna at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the staff was there.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No, no. We were -- Sapna is further than Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we look at page 2 of that document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It's the second marked paragraph, where it says, "The defence of Kula Grad," in English. That paragraph. It's the fourth paragraph: "The defence of Kula Grad, from the 9th to the 26th of April, was carried out while the JNA was still the legal armed force in the region of Tuzla, when the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina had still not named an aggressor, and was not yet organised or ready to conduct a defensive and liberating war. At that time, Kula Grad was the symbol of BH resistance ... Kula Grad showed that resistance was possible," and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, it had to defend itself. There's no question about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But the point here is that the JNA was the legal armed force at the time and that your commanders knew that full well.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, from 1990 onwards, there was no JNA. It could only have been the Serb army. I served the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and we would salute this way, like this. In 1990, the war still hadn't broken out and we were passing by soldiers, and this is the sign, Mr. Karadzic, they made in salute. The Yugoslav Army never saluted in this way. This is how we saluted. This is how I saluted as a JNA soldier. So after the 1990s, don't mention the JNA. The JNA dissolved as soon as the conflict broke out in Slovenia and Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But let's not delve in politics. We have a lot to get through, and it would be better if we could get through it all today. And we'll come to how this army became predominantly Serb, as you say. Looking at the documents that we're going to see today, it is clear that this is an order from your leadership, and I'd like you to focus on the last paragraph on the first page. In English it is: "From the beginning," the last paragraph just before page 2. It says: "From the beginning of the war to the present day, resistance in the wider region of Kamenica was based on preparations carried out, the awareness of the need for combat in the region cut off from the rest of the liberated territories of the municipality, the headquarters of the armed forces, and the leadership of the municipality. "Under those conditions combat was carried out independently in co-operation with the staffs and units of the armed forces of Vlasenica, Bratunac, Srebrenica, in the triangle of Kamenica-Cerska-Srebrenica. The" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I can feel the gasping of the interpreters. Please slow down when you read out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The inhabited parts of the area were independently held. The roads from Mali Zvornik to Ljubovija and Zvornik to Drinjaca were controlled. Mali Zvornik and Drinjaca in Serbia, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So Serbia couldn't go from Mali Zvornik to Ljubovija on its own territory?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness's answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Where could we do that? Where could we prevent Serbia from moving around its own territory? Where? Where were we able to do that? Where you can see that? My village was built up and cut off towards the Drina River. We were in the middle. The others were up towards Sekovici. We were sandwiched between the two.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But let's stick to the document. You have it before you. We're dealing with page 2 now. At the top of page 2 in the Serbian version. Page 2 in the Serbian. It's -- your command states that the inhabited areas of the region were held and that the roads from Zvornik to Ljubovija and Zvornik to Drinjaca were controlled. You didn't have -- control it physically. It can be controlled through firepower.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: How was it controlled if Mali Zvornik is from the bridge running downwards towards Koviljaca? It doesn't run down towards Ljubovija.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see the road from Drinjaca?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And what about from Kula Grad?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, Kula Grad was attacked at the very beginning in April. Kula Grad fell in April. First of all, they didn't have any weapons for them to be able to control it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, I would kindly ask you to provide me with short answers. I'll ask my questions. You give us your answers, and we'll get through your testimony this week. Your report says that they controlled the road as well as the Zvornik-Drinjaca road, which is in Bosnia-Herzegovina; right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Oh, come on let's leave those stories, empty stories.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you can tell your commander that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Leave those empty stories and rumours. They're just rumours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I do have an objection. It's a small point. This witness has explained what his role was guarding his village. To put to the witness that this is "your report" and lump him in somehow with the author of this report or -- is wrong and I think it's provocative. It's not the witness's report and you can't lump everybody together in that manner and say "your report."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. I think the accused understood. Please go on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I will be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is a report from the Muslim command, so that's the sense of it, and my question's along those lines. Now, in the next paragraph it says: "In extended co-operation, Magija's group ... on the 9th of July, 1992, were introduced. Kibe's group, Himzo's group, Nazif's group, on the 27th of July, and some smaller group with ammunition and Medical Corps material, sanitary materials." Now focus on this part of the sentence: "As well as the executed withdrawal of 7.500 civilians from the first half of July to the first half of August."

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: It is true that they pulled out the civilians. That's right. You're right there, because you forced them from Kula Grad, Snagovo, Liplje, and all that general area. You made the population flow into my small, poor village with no communication, and they had to take those people in, otherwise they would have died.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm just asking you if you see that sentence and that it says that throughout the war, furthermore, that efforts were made, through General Morillon and outside General Morillon, to have these civilians evacuated from those areas.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, let me tell you, sir. We were very concerned about our civilians, because the civilians were being killed by shells. More civilians were killed by shells -- more children were killed by shells than bullets, because bullets couldn't reach long distances, whereas shells and grenades could.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But would have they been getting killed if there were no fighting?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. Why were not -- they were not getting killed in 1992. You could get killed in a traffic accident or a worker could fall from a building perhaps.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right. I would like you to look at the paragraph beginning with "Basis of successful resistance." Let us see. The grounds of the successful resistance. It is in English: "The grounds of successful resistance were accredited to the preparations undertaken several months before the war, which were thus reflected in the effectiveness of a large part of the activists, the organised arming, and resolve to offer resistance at any cost. A particular effect in the sustaining of the freedom of the territory was created by the arrival and activity of Captain Hajrudin Mesic who had, together with Captain Mehdin, Senad Hodzic and a smaller number of other organisers of the resistance and the uprising, had managed to create a sense of the need for armed resistance as well as the potential and the effectiveness of freedom fighting. Captain Hajra's group was the first combat unit in this region." Whose captains were these and where was this, in which area?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: In Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, Zvornik is big.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Ask me about my area. Don't ask me where Hajro Mesic was. Had it not been for Hajro Mesic there would have been more, thousands more victims. Had we not been stopping you, as evil as you were, not only would we have 200.000 dead, we would have had 5 -- half a million dead if we had not kept stopping you in your advance.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, had Hajro Mesic not been there or that policy, Bosnia wouldn't be composed of three units now, and your village would now be in the Muslim area and nobody would have been killed. Your village and your area would have been in the Muslim state entity. This is something that we had accepted in March 1992. You convinced the people that you should be ruling it over the Serbs, and Hajro Mesic and others were preparing the war months in advance. This is what I can conclude from your sources, from Muslim sources. My question was: Whose captains were these captains?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Just one moment. Mr. Karadzic, had we not put up any resistance, we would have had half a million casualties, perhaps 200.000, but even more likely half a million. You know what happened to the Srebrenica population. God forbid that there had been 300.000 citizens in Srebrenica. At least 100.000 of them would have been killed. It was only God's will, thanks to God's will that these 10 or 12 people had survived in order to be able to tell their stories here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just -- Mr. Karadzic, this is not an occasion for you to make a conclusion. Just ask questions. And I would like you to move on to other issues, material issues.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I agree with you, but the witness is making statements of a political nature, implying some factual matters as well. Less than 60.000 Muslims were killed. They had 40.000 fighters killed. All of this is different from what has been known so far, and that is why I am asking him to pay attention to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Whose captains were these people before the war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, it is well known that these captains were Muslims. But you know, Mr. Karadzic, that we, Bosnia and Herzegovina, had no army, that we had one single Yugoslav People's Army, and you, Mr. Karadzic, had generals from the beginning. You had tanks. You had planes. You had howitzers, different types of guns. There was no calibre that you didn't have. So can you please explain to us before this Chamber how is it that you had such weaponry?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When I get to testify, I will explain that. Anyway, were these Muslims captains captains of the JNA?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't know. Perhaps they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From which other army would they have been captains of?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't know what they were doing before the war, if they were captains in any army before then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm talking about matters being mentioned in this report, the triangle Kamenica, Cerska, Srebrenica. That's what I'm talking about. My next question is this: On page 3 in the Serbian version and in the English version, it's still on page 2 but it's marked at page 3, we have information about the activities there. Who lived in Brdjani, sir?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Where are Brdjani?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: In your municipality.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't think there is a Brdjani there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who lives in Odzacine?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Serbs, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who lives in Rozanj?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Perhaps Serbs, but I'm not actually that familiar with Rozanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yeah, we did have all of that. It says in this period many combat operations took place from which we will touch upon only a few, the liberation of Sapna and Gaj on May 6th, the battle for Zaseok on the 10th of May, the taking of Brdjani on the 14th of May, Odzacine on the 11th of June, the battle for Boskovici on the 22nd of June, 1992. What did the Muslim army want in Boskovici?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Who attacked Sapna and Gaj? Did the Muslims attack Gaj or did the Serbs do that? Gaj and Sapna are -- have a 90 per cent Muslim population. Can you please explain to me who attacked this Sapna and this Gaj? Did they attack themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who lived in Rastosnica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Serbs lived in Rastosnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There were three Croats in Rastosnica, six Muslims, and 2.334 Serbs. It was a very rich village, it wasn't?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't know. I never saw that village. I just heard about the village, but I heard that there wasn't a single Muslim in Rastosnica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, it says that on the 19th of August, 1992, and you were in your village then, the liberation of Rastosnica took place. Who was it liberated from?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Look, let me tell you this: Don't ask me that. Ask witnesses who are from that area if they come here. I have nothing to do with Rastosnica. It's 40 kilometres away from me. I was struggling to protect my children and my family. I wasn't going off to liberate Rastosnica. I don't even know where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. But you know everything that was going on your village, don't you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes. You can ask me about my village. Don't ask me anything outside my village. I'm not a military analyst to be able to -- well, look, I came here without a single piece of paper with me. I didn't write any history of the war. All I can say is that we were defending ourselves. We didn't have the strength to attack.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, all the offensive actions and the occasional defensive one are noted here. So you were assaulting, attacking.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Whom?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, who were your enemies in that war?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Those who were attacking us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Who was that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: It was Serbs. They were attacking us, and they were our enemies, of course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm objecting to the argumentative nature of some of this. Occasionally there's an actual question, but we're also getting things like, "So you were assaulting, attacking." It's not a question. It's a statement to the witness. I realise this is cross-examination but he should be asking questions to the witness about topics the witness can talk about and topics that he knows about. And the witness is trying to make clear what areas he can talk about and what parts he just doesn't know about. But it's not helpful, I think, to make these argumentative assertions that don't even contain a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. And sir -- and, Mr. Witness, on your part as well, just hear out the question and then try to maintain your answer to be simple as much as possible. Mr. Karadzic, continue, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I can believe Mr. Nicholls that this is a cross-examination that is detrimental to the Prosecution, but that is the goal of my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, don't try to make a final statement, final comment. Please continue. Just concentrate on questioning.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at page 4. Page 4 in the Serbian. It's probably page 4 in the English, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At the bottom of the page, sir -- well, at the top it says, "Organisational establishment structure of the units," and there we have the units listed. We can look at the table at the bottom, an overview of the units, fighters, the number of the fighters, interventions, positions, rear.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Actually, it's probably page 4 in the English. In the B/C/S it's page -- in the English it's page 5. In the B/C/S it's page 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: So we have a total of 32 units, and the staff. Do you see this list, sir?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: What are you thinking of when you say 32 units? Are you thinking of 32 units only in my village or in the entire Zvornik municipality area?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik municipality area.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, don't ask me about the Zvornik municipality. You can only ask me about my area. I did not adopt or conduct any military policies. You all have papers. I'm talking only about things that I remember. I'm not interested about what happened in Sapna, in Djulici, what happened in Bijeljina. This is something that I don't know because they are removed from me. I didn't communicate by telephone with anybody who could then tell me over the telephone this and this happened in such and such a place.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, look at number 20. This is on page 5 in the Serbian. Did you hear about the unit called Mosque Doves or pigeons? Did you ever hear about that unit?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No, I never heard of that unit.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 5 in the Serbian, and also I think we would need to move to the following page in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, can you look at this last unit with the name Sultan Fatih. Does this refer to Mehmed the Conqueror who conquered Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, if you believe me, this is the first time that I'm hearing that there was a unit with such a name. I'm hearing it now, from you, for the first time. I hadn't heard of that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now look at the following page, please. And the next page in the English as well, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now we can see the replenishment: Communications equipment, 30 per cent; infantry armament, 40 per cent; support armament, 30 per cent; anti-armour weaponry, 20 per cent; motor vehicles, 45 per cent; equipment and so on and so forth. Do you see that? So infantry weaponry 40 per cent. So there's more than enough for three shifts if the weapons are not taken home but left at the positions; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: All I could have had would have been infantry weapons. There were no trucks, auxiliary arms, vehicles. You know that we didn't have any gas stations to supply ourselves. I mean, even if you had a car you were unable to drive it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please look at page 8 now, please. Excuse me, no, we need to look at page 7. We are on page 7. Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: On this page you can see what was required, what needed to be procured. Do you see that? Because I don't need to read it, perhaps. RUPs, Motorolas, modern infantry weaponry, jackets, uniforms, small calibre ammunition, and so on.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Who was asking for this and who could have provided that? Can you please tell me how far Tuzla is from this area? You were holding all of this territory. Tuzla didn't have any links with this village of ours or the villages of ours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is your local unit asking for supplies from the base, but let us go back to the previous page.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's look at page 8 in the B/C/S. I think in the English it's also page 8. Actually, in the English it's probably one more page. We're looking at the end of the document. The last page in the English, the last page of the document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And it says: "Central tasks for the further development of the armed forces of the municipality." We're going to skip that. We're going to move to the second paragraph. The main tasks are equipping with winter equipment and materiels and technical equipment. The organisational and formational rearranging of units and the vital enforcing of order, soldier discipline and organisation. In the matter of command and control the key tasks are the filling of chief positions, reinforcement, leading and forming of the district staff of Kamenica, and the improvement of the system of communications. "With the conduct of combat operations, the focus should be directed at the operations to liberate and open the corridor toward Kamenica, enabling us to maintain the corridor and to strengthen the frontal area of the defence, the forward area of defence throughout the liberated territory."

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: All right, Karadzic. What are you trying to say when you say it was like this? Did you want to say that we were not supposed to fight at all, that we should have been sitting at home, and when you come we would have allowed you to assemble all of us in one building for you to rape the women and the girls, to kill whoever you wanted, to release who you wanted, to do with the people as you wanted? This is what you perhaps wanted, but the people had at least a little bit of sense to put up some resistance. There was one single camp in our area and it was the only one that we liberated. And perhaps, if you want, I can explain to the Trial Chamber all the things that went on in that camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's take it document by document and try and be as precise as possible. Now, in your units, in your -- did you have people from other parts, for example, Albanians?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: We really are talking about things that don't hold water. Well, we had enough men but not enough weapons. We didn't need more people to come in. Had we had the necessary weapons, we could have defended ourselves and this would never have happened. I would be sitting in my house at home and you wouldn't have set fire to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We're wasting time, Witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm asking -- I was talking, Witness. The question was about the people, whether there was some -- you have people from other parts, for example, Albanians, but your answer was regarding the weapons. So could you try to answer the question and keep your answers as simple as possible, please. Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were there any Albanians in Kamenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: No Albanian women either?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No, nobody.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have Defence Exhibit 1D00639 next, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: While we are bringing that document, following the procedure, are you minded to tender that document into evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly, Your Excellency.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How about the map, the Cutileiro map? Are you -- were you also minded to tender it or you are minded to tender it at a later stage?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can do that later, because it wasn't precise enough. It wasn't a precise Cutileiro map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. We'll admit this report, and the number is?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D38.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we have Defence document 639 now, please. It hasn't been translated, but we'll do our best to explain the substance of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know this boy from your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, he seems familiar. It's a child. I'm not quite sure, but I would say he was familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now may we have page 2 of this document displayed, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, as Mr. Karadzic said, I don't know -- this isn't translated. I don't know what it's going to say, but if we're showing pictures of people that are from the witness's village, then I think we need to go into private session, if we're going to show pictures, stories that identify the village, or at a minimum not broadcast the image.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Let's proceed without broadcasting this image for the moment. Yes, thank you. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May we have page number 2, please. And could it not be publicly displayed. I'll read it, but on Sanction, please. I don't wish this to be broadcast, just for the courtroom. Number 3. I would like page number 3. No. I'm sorry, page 4. That's right. I need page 4, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I will read it, omitting the name of the village and just saying "your village." (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) He tried to save his dog and paid with his life for -- in the attempt." And I'll explain what happened. Since this considerable minority in your village felt themselves to be under threat, fled during the night, and this little boy Slobodan remembered that he'd left behind his little dog, Lassie, and nobody could prevent him from going to untie his dog and take the dog with him. When he returned, he came across your army there, and Elfete Veseli, this woman, was a member of that army, and the boy never returned but not as you and other witnesses have said, we've never seen the person coming back with the man, we don't know what happened to the man, but here, unfortunately, we have testimony about what happened to Slobodan. Ilija goes on to say: "We lived in that village of yours. The Muslims were in the majority in the village. For days and nights we sat around devising a plan of escape because we saw what the Serbs would suffer. It was Thursday, the 4th of June, 1992, when, at dawn, we seized an opportunity and managed to get out. We took four or five goats with us. We found refuge in a hamlet," and I won't mention the hamlet, "with one of the -- with a kum of Zoran Milosevic. It's along the Drina River. When we arrived, Slobodan said, 'Daddy, Lassie has stayed behind, tethered,' and he went down to save the dog." And let's see what happened to Slobodan next. His father goes on to say nobody could prevent him from going to save his dog --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, there's no point in reading out all parts of the media article. Just put your question. What is your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very sorry to rise again. Just -- just to be careful. Page 70, lines 1 to 5, I think if we redact. He's talking about the names of the person in the village of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll come to my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "'My son Slobodan's arms were cut off to the elbow,' his father recounts. 'Not a single finger was -- toe was left on his feet. His ears had been cut off. There was a wound cut into his chest in the form of a square, and his skin had been stripped back. There was -- were traces of an entrance/exit wound on his head.'" Witness, you were in the village at the time. Do you know about this event?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) They could have gone anywhere they wanted. Now, what happened to the boy, I don't know. Whether somebody sent him, I can't say. I don't know what the boy did. I didn't see the boy. I knew the boy because they lived nearby. I'm not saying that they didn't, and they weren't bad neighbours either, for that matter. But as soon as the multi-party elections were completed, there's that man, what was his name, Sumbulja [phoen] was his nickname. He was the only one to stay with us and he died a year ago, but he was the only one to stay behind. Otherwise, nobody else remained. But nobody expelled them. They decided to leave of their own accord. Now, what they did with their child, I don't know. There was some scouting going on. Now, a mother and father, to let their son go back to save a dog, I don't think so. I don't think so. There was something else afoot.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we'll come to Slobodan and his parents and the punishment that ensued, but you were talking about the elections. What were you saying?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, this Sumbulja man, I can't remember what his name was, but him and this Stojanovic family, they started beating him because he said he voted for Alija, and they probably voted for the SDS. So they swore at him for voting for Alija.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And they disclosed themselves in that way, right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, they quarreled.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: -- interrupt again, but we have names again on page 71 at lines 20 and 21. It may be impossible to talk about this incident. Maybe we should go into private session if it's going to continue to go into detail about this incident and different names, because otherwise we're going to keep reacting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, I'm seeing those lines as well. We'll move on to other issues. If we continue to --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I'm not going to mention names. It would be a good idea for Mr. Nicholls to prevail upon his witness to refrain from stating place names and the names of people, but I would like us to stay in open session, if possible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So, sir, Mr. Witness, be cautious when naming other people because it may reveal your -- your town. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, all right. Everybody knows about the place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I'm seeing the clock -- let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that this sweet little boy deserved this kind of death?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, all right, he didn't deserve it, but thousands of children of other ethnicities did not deserve the death that they met, and you're not asking about them, Mr. Karadzic. The women and girls and the peoples whose whole families were killed. I'm not justifying this. She shouldn't have done anything to the child. But what happened to her -- her family? She was an Albanian woman. What happened to her family in Vlasenica? Why don't you ask them in Vlasenica whether her family had been killed first?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, she was part of the BH Army, and it was on that basis that she happened to be in your village at that time and committed this act, and nobody is challenging that, and this dangerous boy coming to reconnoiter, as you put it, was cut into pieces.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, we heard that the child had been killed, but nobody said that the child had been massacred.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I'd like to tender this Defence document into evidence, please. Rather, I'd like to have it MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honours. We just, of course, wait for the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be MFI D39, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll have a break now, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, when you filed the notifications of time estimate for April 2010 on 9th of April this year, you indicated you would need four hours for cross-examination of this witness. At the time you didn't indicate that four hours would be necessary, only for the purpose of the situation regarding '92 -- '93. Given that you spent about -- more than one and a half hours as of now for the cross-examination but you haven't dealt with a thing about the situation in '95. During the course of next session I would expect you to come to those issues. We have a witness who testifies -- who survived one of the horrendous massacres, but you made an appalling statement that he's not a victim but just a soldier. You should come to your questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, excuse me. If we could move into private session very quickly before you adjourn. I wanted to raise one matter, bring it to the Court's attention.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, I had counted on what Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff had stated, that Srebrenica would come at the end, and even if I don't have time to say anything about 1995, I'd like to clarify the events leading up to 1993, because that's so important. It's very important that nobody asks this witness relevant questions and he's angry now. And I don't want to insult him. He's insulted by the truth, but I'm insulted by lies and I have to clear this up.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So I would like --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: This is not an opportunity for you to make submissions. You will have full opportunities. So concentrate on your questions. And -- nobody -- the Chamber has not precluded you from asking questions regarding 1992, 1993 questions -- situations, but given your statement -- given the case, I think it's proper for you to use your time properly. We will rise for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Excellency.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, you came on the 3rd of April. Did you hear that Mr. Izetbegovic, as the president of our joint Presidency, declared general mobilisation on the 4th of April for the entire combat force in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this was in the media.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you watch television in your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes, I did, but I never heard that this happened then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And did you hear that on the 8th of April, mobilisation of the Muslim sector of the police was declared in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I think that that was when Zvornik fell. The Serbian forces took Zvornik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The mobilisation took place first, then the Serbs fled to Serbia.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: And then when did they come?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at 643 now, please. 643 is in English. We need to look at page 2 of 643. It's only in English. We don't have it in the Serbian here. Ah, it's in the e-court in Serbian too. I'm going to deal with the text in English and the interpreters can translate it for you. This is page 55. Page 55 -- actually, page 69 of the book, and page 5 of the English document. In e-court it's page 9, and in the Serbian it's page 69.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: While we're waiting, I'm going to read to you something from the first paragraph, where it says: "[In English] The SDA aspired to create a single front, and it gains the support of all except the SDS. With the conflict in Croatia, more specifically when conflict erupted in Pakrac, spring 1991, Brano Grujic, the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS, had requested a meeting of creating a strategy to prevent the conflict from translating to Zvornik. The meeting was held, and it was agreed that the situation would be monitored so that this region would remain in a peaceful state." [Interpretation] You can see that the president of the Serbian Democratic Party, Brano Grujic, made the first move by offering to create conditions so that the war would not move into Zvornik; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No, definitely not. The tanks were in Karakaj on the 2nd and 3rd of April. What you say about the Serbs crossing into Serbia is incorrect.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you. Please, I ask you not to waste my time.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Brano Grujic knew that he was being tried for war crimes or that he would be tried for war crimes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. Just for the record and for the witness, could the accused put on the record what -- what he's actually reading from. It's not in the transcript, I don't believe. The book and the author.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. You omitted introducing the foundation of the book, who was the author, what it is about. Let's continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, Excellency, I didn't forget. This is my tactic that I use with hostile witnesses.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, this is a book by Mirza Hamzic. The title of the book is "Zvornik from elections to Dayton." It was published in 1998. You've heard the name of Mirza Hamzic before, haven't you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But definitely he's Muslim. Is he a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes, judging by the first and last name, yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your permission, I would like to continue. We would need to look at page 10 of this document and page 71 of the book now. In English you -- you have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "The Patriotic League was formed on the July the 26th, 1991, in a youth library in Kula Grad. We had formed a Crisis Staff, but its commander was yet to be chosen. In the conversations between Hadzic and Juzbasic, it was requested that Juzbasic's wing should deliver a commander. A meeting was held during which it was decided that Sakib Halilovic, aka Kibe, was to be named as a -- as the commander." [Interpretation] Do you know Sakib Halilovic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The next paragraph: "[In English] The organisation was now created. The defence plan was created, and a network for weapon delivery was established. Weapons were purchased in Vienna and delivered to Brod, where the network of the Patriotic League was formed. 'Smugglers' were brought in who had sold weapons in order to be able to purchase new ones. In September of 1991, roughly 15 weapons had arrived via the SDA, which had a counter-effect because Juzbasic had been saying how weapons should not be purchased and how the SDA would arm the people."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 11 of the document now, please, and page 72 of the book. Excellencies, I think you have that on this page. The last part of the paragraph there says -- I have to read the whole paragraph: "[In English] Through companies there were attempts to access money for the purchasing of weapons. During one meeting with company executives, when the Chetniks tore through Serbia, had begun their bacchanalia in Karakaj and Celopek, means were sought but Muhamed Jelkic, the executive manager of the health centre" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Next page in B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "Had offered to supply the means necessary for the purchasing of weapons by which the people would be protected. Accordingly, there was a topic on the withdrawal of our young men serving in the JNA, and the prevention of the mobilisation of reservists." [Interpretation] I asked you, sir, whether the JNA became Serb because Serbs were rushing to join the JNA or because you were leaving the JNA and preventing mobilisation pursuant to instructions from your leaders.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Had there been Bosniaks in the army, it was referred to as the JNA from the 1990s, they would have been victims. They probably would have had to be at forward positions, your Serb soldiers would be behind them, and in shooting they would probably have been the victims.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was not my question. The question was whether Muslim soldiers and officers were leaving the JNA pursuant to instructions of your leadership, and did your leadership prevent the response to the call-up?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes, it did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now move to the next page, please. "[In English] Conflict with the SDA had influenced the effectiveness of this action. At one point, the Zvornik MUP had encountered one of our soldiers in the JNA who had deserted and returned him to his unit. As a response to question as to what he was doing, Osman Mustafic, MUP executive, had answered, I am sustaining the legal government. And what are we doing? You are creating an upheaval." [Interpretation] A rebellion. An overthrow. An overthrow, a rebellion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you hear of Osman Mustafic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Were the overall preparations of the Muslim community and their fighting have the character of a rebellion?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But this policeman, a government figure, said you are conducting an overthrow.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, he said that about the SDA.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. This is what the Serbs were doing. Osman was just a pawn. He couldn't do anything there. You immediately separated and set up barricades around Karakaj, together with the Serbian police. Osman could only have just watched this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, you are wasting time. We already lost a lot of time on some other questions.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: You are wasting time. I can sit here for as long as necessary.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I know, but the Chamber won't permit that.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, it's up to you, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: "[In English] The result was a paradoxical situation in which Pasic's faction was well controlled by the MUP, whose leader was a Bosniak. In spite of that fact, the SDA had, through channels of the Patriotic League, managed to import around 3 or 4.000 barrels to the municipality of Zvornik. At one of the Assembly sessions of the municipality Zvornik, the SDS representative had presented information of the arming of the Bosniaks. Inspector Sakib Coric," [Interpretation] who is evidently a Muslim, "[In English] was hired to examine the status and was given a warrant to apprehend Asim Hadzic as the organiser of the illegal activity -- of that illegal activity. Hadzic had managed to acquire that warrant and had given it to the republic MUP minister, Alija Delimustafic." [Interpretation] Sir, do you see that there was political activity in the municipality to prevent the arming, but this was bypassed and this was something that went past Delibasic, who is a Muslim police officer?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, you are reading this and that, but I'm really familiar with very little of what you are reading out.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we're in a hurry, so let us go to page 73 of the book, the end of that paragraph, where it says: "[In English] Abdulah Pasic had answered, Surrender the weapons. I had already contacted the other side and we need to continue living together." [Interpretation] Abdulah Pasic also believes that we should live together and not to fight. Have you heard of Abdulah Pasic?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: You know what? What you are saying, we did surrender weapons, and those people who did surrender their weapons are dead now. They didn't get to cohabit with the others just because they handed over their weapons. What you are saying is actually not accurate at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is accurate. Page 12 and page 74 of the book: "[In English] The employees of Radio Zvornik were told to pack the equipment and abandon the city, and that the municipal authorities were to move to Kula Grad." [Interpretation] So the Muslim part of the authorities in Zvornik municipality were leaving Zvornik and transferring to Kula Grad, the centre of authority.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Oh, come on, Karadzic. Don't say such stupid things. Please don't. Kula Grad can't take the -- they left Zvornik municipality. If you have something more intelligent to say, say it, but don't keep on about stupid things like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, don't get upset. This is a Serb truth.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: It's the Serb untruth. Mr. Karadzic, tell this Court and the people here, please tell them. Do you acknowledge that the Serbs were responsible for anything and should be held responsible for anything? It's only others that are to blame, according to you. But let's stop these stupidities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Sir. Sir, could you be so kind to simply answer the question. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I can't answer stupid questions. I do apologise. You're the President, but I experienced everything on my own skin, and my children were not able to have a happy childhood like other children. So if you don't like what I'm saying, just tell me. You can tell me, "Sir, you can leave and go back to where you came from."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, you've come here to answer the questions, and in that way, the Chamber is assisted in finding the truth. So I can understand how you feel, but please calm down and then concentrate on answering the questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, you tell him not to read this because it's got nothing to do with me. He can read something that is personally linked to me. I'm not a military strategist and I didn't write an archive so that I can open documents like Karadzic can with his associates and do it that way. I'm just telling you what I know about. I'm not interested in anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So please bear with the question, and if you are not able to answer the question or you don't know anything about it, please answer in that way. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, they're not questions for me. They're not questions for me. Not my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, in your statements and during your testimony, you did make claims about what happened in that area, and now I want to show that what happened were other things, and I'm reading a Muslim source. This isn't an attack against you. It's just an attempt to establish the truth.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: There's not one iota of truth there, so don't talk about the truth. That's why I am getting upset, because you're telling untruths, and I thank Allah for having been in Bosnia and Herzegovina throughout the war so I could see, come to realise what my neighbours were like. They had dinner with us one night and took up knives to kill us the other.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And is that the first time in our history that that happened, Witness?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, it is as far as I'm concerned, because I don't remember other historical events. But this happened before the eyes of the world, before the United Nations, and the United Nations linked up the Bosniak people and gave the executioners all their weapons. Gentlemen, you know that Srebrenica was a protected area, and it should not have fallen, and you allowed 18.000 inhabitants to be killed. Did you hear a mother saying last year that she was in childbirth in Potocari, and another woman helped her deliver her baby, and as soon as the baby let out a cry, a Serb soldier came out and smothered the child, killed the child. You don't understand that, gentlemen. When the mothers of Srebrenica said they were going to sue the United Nations, they said the United Nations had immunity. Nobody had such strong immunity, because you took away -- first of all, you took away all our property. Then you took away our lives, and now you want to say that we Muslims wanted --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: Excuse me. Excuse me. Now, we fully -- we fully appreciate how you feel. We really do. But now what Judge Morrison and Judge Kwon have said, I will also say. Dr. Karadzic is entitled to ask you questions. He is entitled to cross-examine you. If when you hear the question you find you don't understand it, then let us know. We'll have him clarify it. If the question is improper, then the Prosecutor would object. We would hear the objection, and we will rule, or we ourselves might intervene. But as long as the question has not been objected to, and as long as we haven't intervened and you understand the question, answer it as best you can. That is all we are saying. But we do appreciate how you feel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge, sir -- Judge, sir, I understand you. I understand you well, but you don't understand me. You're listening to what Karadzic is reading, and that has nothing to do with my statement or testimony. I'm not interested in that. I'm not a politician. I'm not a military analyst.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: You see, what I'm saying is this: If when Mr. Karadzic asks you a question you don't agree, say, "I don't agree." If you don't accept it, say "I don't accept it." But you see, you can't tell him that he can't ask you. He is entitled to cross-examine. But you now would be entitled to say, "Look, I don't understand this question --"

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have my rights too. I have come here to did testify --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: You, indeed, have your rights. You do indeed have your rights and we would not allow those rights to be trampled on, but he also has his rights. And we are there now to balance, to ensure that both sets of rights are respected. Mr. Karadzic, let's carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BAIRD
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Let's go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, I'm going to make it easier for everyone concerned, and I won't read word for word, but I'd like to say something with respect to page 16, page 82 of the book, that after the meeting with Mr. Mustafic, Captain Dragan Obrenovic arrived and informed them that an incident had taken place. I think that was the 5th of April, an incident in Sapna where a soldier of the Yugoslav People's Army, which with -- withdrawing to Yugoslavia was killed, and the other soldiers were scattered and eight of their soldiers were captured. Do you remember that incident?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. The president of the municipality, Abdulah Pasic and the SDA, Asim Juzbasic, proposed that the soldiers be released to prevent an escalation. Did you hear about that happening?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let's move on to page 26 now, which is page 102 of the book. And there Mr. Hamzic, this is Mirza Hamzic's book and his words, he said that they were thinking about calling their army the Muslim army. Did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: In our army there were people of all ethnicities. It wasn't a mono-ethnic army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, we had whole Muslim units in our army.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't believe that. I don't believe that. And if you did, perhaps you had prisoners to dig trenches for you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now let's look at page 30 of this document and it is page 111 of the book.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 111 says the following: "We had a plan for defence, for the defence of Zvornik, and we had information from the authorities in Zvornik, and they were Muslims, said Almir, because the former JNA just crossed the Zvornik in Serbia [In English] arranged artillery, fortified itself and brought more reinforcements. Thus, immediately prior to the Chetnik aggression, we had intended to occupy the key positions in Zvornik. Assuredly, however, we are not able to do so without the support and co-operation of the leading figures in municipality." [Interpretation] It says here that before the Serb attack, they moved the radio and the Muslim authorities to Kula Grad, and they planned to take control of the key positions in town. Now, did you hear about that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. They didn't have the force and strength to do that with the cause. Serbia raised their cause. How could the population fight the Serbian cause, army cause?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm sure the Trial Chamber will calculate the time spent on nothing, my time spent on nothing. "According to the plan Zvornik was not to be defended alone. [In English] It was only one of the municipalities for which commander Sakib Halilovic was installed in the subregion of Podrinje which was, aside from Zvornik, also comprised of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Vlasenica, and Kladanj, and the commander was Salko Dedic." [Interpretation] So the regional military organisation whose commander was Salko Delic -- Dedic. Now, when I said previously that it wasn't the Serb truth, what I meant -- what I said is this is a Muslim truth. So I'd like to correct the transcript on that score. Was there regional military organisation as Mirza Hamzic writes in the book?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Zvornik, Bratunac, Kladanj, Vlasenica, and so on. The commander was Salko Dedic.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers kindly be asked to speak one at a time for the benefit of one and all, otherwise it is impossible to interpret. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, just a second. The interpreters couldn't follow your questions and answers because you were overlapping at the same time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll repeat it if they haven't interpreted it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Prosecution instruct the witness that it is me asking the questions and not him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The Prosecution has nothing to do with monitoring the witness evidence. It is for the Chamber. The last question was: "Zvornik, Bratunac, Kladanj, Vlasenica, and so on. The commander was Salko Dedic." That's what we have in the transcript. What is your answer, Mr. Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, this is the first time that I hear of this man Salko Dedic, and I was in an encirclement. I had no communication with anyone or anything.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I continue, Your Excellency?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Page 36 of this document, and page 123 of the book. It -- "[In English] Salko Bukarevic, one of the organisers and active members of the Patriotic League for north-eastern Bosnia recalls this period retrospectively." [No interpretation]. "At the beginning of January 1992, Sefer Halilovic, the commander of Patriotic League for B and H, arrived in Tuzla from Sarajevo. Together with the members of the headquarters of the Patriotic League Tuzla, he visited the north-eastern Bosnia region. Among the members of the headquarters was also Salko Bukarevic, who says about the -- Sefer's visit." [Interpretation] Page 37 or 124: "[In English] Talks with the leader of SDA and municipality authorities --" [Interpretation] So the municipal authorities, the Muslim part of the municipal authorities are collaborating with the illegal Patriotic League in January 1992, the beginning of January 1992. On that occasion he gave specific tasks for individual municipalities. [In English] He was especially interested in the readiness of Podrinje for a potential defence. That is when the president of the SDS Zvornik, Asim Juzbasic said that all units are ready for a possible task and also that everything is prepared for the destruction of bridges on the Drina." [Interpretation] Sir, you had even prepared the destruction of the bridges on the Drina River in June 1992, whereas we were in the throes of negotiations which ended on the 18th of March with the exceptions of the Lisbon Agreement. Is that the case, is that right or not?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Tell me, Karadzic. What were they prepared -- preparing to defend themselves from? Was there a threat to them, that they should prepare themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, does it say that they were prepared, that everything was prepared for the destruction of the bridges?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't know, but what is it that they had to defend themselves against? So if you weren't in favour of war, why would they have to defend themselves and prepare themselves for defence? Answer me that. The Judges are there. The two of you are over there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. Let's not waste time. I'm not here to answer questions, you are.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I'd like to tender this document into evidence, Mirza Hamzic's book, and the excerpts we've read out. 1D00643 is the number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, no real objection. However, I think it should be marked at this time, because we have very small extracts of translation, not a proper translation. We don't have the context of these questions, but I have no real objection. I just don't think we have a proper translation at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Despite the Prosecution's observation, the Chamber is not minded to admit this book. The reason is because most of the part -- the contents were put to the witness, and the witness did not confirm most of those parts. The part that the witness confirmed is -- has been already reflected in the transcript, so there's no need for those parts to be admitted separately. And as far as these other parts the witness didn't confirm or did not agree with, there is no basis. That does not mean that you cannot produce it during the Defence case. So this shows how much you wasted time. I would expect you to get advice from Mr. Robinson how to use your cross-examination time wisely and efficiently. This is not a proper way of cross-examination, in particular, to the witness, as you said, who is not hostile -- who is not friendly to you. So please bear that in mind. So this exhibit is not admitted at this moment. Move on to your next topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. I think that this exhibit, if nothing, is useful in order to test the credibility of this witness. Now I would like to call up 644, and could I please ask that it not be broadcast to the public. 644. And can we prepare 645? We're going to go through them quickly. I just would like for the witness to look at this and comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do we not go -- do we not need to go into private session?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. If this is not being broadcast outside, then it's not necessary. If this is only being broadcast in the courtroom, then it's all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you know this personality, and do you see his name?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did you socialise with him in Belgrade? He also worked in Belgrade?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. He was in the police and I was in construction. Sometimes we would travel by bus together.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I'm only going to look at the middle paragraph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I please ask you to scroll up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Where it says: "He was one of the first founders of the 1st Muslim Podrinje Brigade, and he joined the same with over (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: (redacted) He carried out officer duties and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document for admission and we will translate it. We will have -- we did not mention the name of the village. Can we please ask the witness although -- the interpreters, although they have to look at the document. This is the village of this witness and this man together, and I have maintained the confidentiality.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, again there's no translation, so I have no idea what Mr. Karadzic is reading from. And two, there hasn't been any statement of what this text in the box is, where it's from. There needs to be some sort of foundation or description of the document rather than just a picture and text in a box that is being admitted. Sought to be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, what is this document about? Who prepared or produced this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, this is a monograph of the 8th Srebrenica Operations Group of the 28th Division of the land forces, which is already in the EDS and in the e-court. It's in the e-court. We're going to look at it. This is number 646. These are all just excerpts in order for us not to have to submit the entire document. We are just bringing up certain portions of this monograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you please tell me, where exactly did he bring these 500 people? The 1st Muslim Podrinje brigade.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: But where? Where? Where? You said from which village he took them, but where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: He took them probably to Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. He left our village before the women and children left. He went to Tuzla. He perhaps didn't even see Srebrenica, ever, with his own eyes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, it states here that he was appointed commander of the 1st Motorised Infantry Brigade. Perhaps it was in Tuzla but --

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Definitely not. I'm not saying anything about Tuzla, but for sure, he never went to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's fine. So, Mr. Nicholls, what is your position having heard from the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I'm still not clear. I'm trying to find out what the document is. It may be in EDS, but I'm not clear on what the document is, where it is, who the author is, what entity it's from.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. It may not be necessary to go into private session if the Court will look quickly at 95, lines 10 through 15. Although the document wasn't broadcast, there were two consecutive references that -- that effectively nullified that cautionary measure, and I think gave indications that should be redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That will be taken care of by the Court Officer and the Legal Officer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [No interpretation] [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, this is a Muslim source, a monograph about their own army after the war. It's loaded into the EDS and the e-court, and in order not to admit or tender the whole document, we are just bringing up certain portions of the documents. So 646 and then 645, and we can look at the first page of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, I would take your word, but you are not giving evidence, and we are not satisfied with the foundation of the document of this kind, so until that time and pending translation, we'll mark this document for identification. What number will be given to this?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI D40, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, did you have something to say? Did you want to say something to me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let's proceed, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just briefly, can we show the witness 645, and 646 after that, and then we're going to move to a different topic. 645 first, please. I would like this not to be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we look at the name. Are you familiar with this name, sir?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Go up.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, do you know this man?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see in the second paragraph it says: "From September 1991, worked intensively to organise and prepare resistance to the aggression on the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina when he was also appointed as commander of the Crisis Staff for the region."

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: That man is still working as a clerk in a municipality. He had nothing to do with the army or anything. I don't think that he ever even went out anywhere or took up a rifle in his hands.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This is a document of your command.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: If we had more people like this, we would have been many, many more dead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellency, can we adopt this -- admit this as an MFI document, and can we please now move to document 646.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. D41, MFI'd. Next one, Exhibit D41, MFI'd.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 646, please. This is the book, the monograph, the 2nd Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Now let us look at 646, page 3, in the e-court. Excellencies, this is that book. It is undoubtedly a Muslim book, published by their army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, will you permit me just to read what --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your question to -- regarding the previous image?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
