utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question was whether he knew this man, and I read the second paragraph where we can see that from September 1991 he worked to organise and prepare armed resistance and so on and so forth. And the witness confirmed that he knew the person but that he doubts or does not believe that he did that and that he was unfit.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He was not unfit. He just didn't join the army. I don't know if he did anything illegally, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What was your question regarding that flag, if that's a -- monograph.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excellencies, that is the cover page of the book from which we are taking this document. Now we're looking at page 3, that I'm going to put questions to the witness from. It's just that I didn't say, "Can we look at page 3." They immediately showed the cover page or page 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Witness, sir, now I'm going to read to you this 8th Operations Group of Srebrenica, later the 28th Division of the ground forces comprise the 280th East Bosnian Light Brigade Potocari, 281st East Bosnian Light Brigade Suceska, 282nd East Bosnian Light Brigade Srebrenica 123, 285th East Bosnian Light Brigade Zepa, 286th Mountain Brigade Srebrenica. You are right, the first Motorised Infantry Brigade was in Tuzla, whose commander was shown on that first picture. So can you please tell us according to what you know, were these units part of the 8th Operations Group?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't know if they were that after 1993, but before 1993, they were not. I actually came to Srebrenica in 1993.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 46 in the e-court? 1C6th Detachment Srebrenica, where it says already in April, the 6th of April, 1992, repelled a Chetnik attack on Kula as well as the surrender of weapons on the 11th of April, 1992, and repelled the Chetnik attack on Kamenica on the 25th of April, 1992. This was followed by attacks on Kula and the fall of Kula, the attack on Snagovo, Liplje and Kamenica. So that is that unit. The retaking of the village and the fighting on the 25th of May, 1992, and the 27th of May, 1992. Sabotage on enemy vehicles and force in Redzici and so on and so forth. I don't want to read to whole thing just look at that. Are you aware of all these fights?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But all of this is happening in your village?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: All I know is that these units came with light vehicles, and I don't know about the rest.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at page 12 in the e-court and can we not broadcast it outside the courtroom again, please. Page 12, TO, the 6th Detachment. I'm not mentioning the name of the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the third line, 4, 5, 6, and you can see your last name on positions 3, 6, and 9. These are commanders of your 6th Detachment from your village.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Yes. What commanders? These are just regular people. It's just that they went to defend the innocent people there. These are no commanders. Not one of them has any rank.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Thank you. You said in your statement that from Konjevic Polje, that it was agreed that civilians should go to Srebrenica from Konjevic Polje. Who was this agreement made with?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Morillon came there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who did Morillon reach this agreement with?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: With Naser Oric.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And who else?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't know. I was just small fry. I don't know who they made these agreements with.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Why didn't he agree about it with Serbs, because the Serbs were supposed to let you cross that territory?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Which Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Serbs from Bratunac and Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, had the Serbs been there, we wouldn't have been able to leave. There was a camp there also. You came there.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're under the pressure of time. I apologise to the interpreters. I understand completely.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You arrived in Srebrenica and Serbs did not take Srebrenica. Why didn't they do that? What do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, you can ask that question to the Serbs. Please don't ask me.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection, Your Honour. I mean, calling for him to speculate why a military action did not take place then.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It is not for the witness to speculate. I agree. Mr. Karadzic, how much longer do you have for this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, I don't think I had more than two hours of effective work. Everything else was procedural questions and resistance from this hostile witness. So I would like to be given two hours, perhaps an hour and a half I could spend with 1995, and then perhaps the witness wouldn't have to come back again.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I see the time. At least I would expect you to start your questions regarding the 1995 circumstances. Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'll do my best, but there are many documents that I haven't gone through. This witness is more important, as far as the Defence is concerned, for 1993. May we now have 255, a Defence exhibit, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I meant tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ah, I beg your pardon. Tomorrow. Right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Before we move on, shall we deal with this document? You're moving on to another document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellencies, yes, I would like to move it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I forgot to mention the previous document which was admitted as D41, MFI'd, was under seal. And this monograph, what would you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I have no objection to this being marked, Your Honour. I'm still not entirely clear what it is, but I'll --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But my concern is that I noted in -- from the e-court, it's of 135 pages long, and the pages which were put to the witness is only 1, 3, 12, and 46. So we will only mark only those pages for identification, pending translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be MFI'd D42, under seal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I fear that more pages were put to the witness than you mentioned. Pages on e-court or pages in the book, which?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I relied on you when I referred to page numbers, but that can be clarified after checking the transcript. Let's go on. So I was advised that they are e-court numbers.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I hope we'll be able to correct it if necessary. May we have the next document. Do we have time for that one today, one more?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have ten more minutes for today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1D0055 [as interpreted] is the next document, please. 255 is the document number. I don't know how it was interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Now, Witness -- may we zoom in. You have my order of the 16th of April, 1993, there, and it says: "I hereby order cease all operations of the army --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think the witness can read it. Do you recognise any of the document? Can you read them? No.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I'm not trying to read it either, because I need my glasses to read. I can't even read one or two lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We can put it on the overhead projector, if you like, and I'll read it.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, you go ahead and read it. I don't need to read it. No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From this order we can see that I ordered that all operations cease against Srebrenica. And then one item says that I also ordered that no investigations of the crime be undertaken, committed by those soldiers, the Muslim soldiers, so as to prevent increased tension. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Well, you might have ordered it for the benefit of the public, but secretly you said, "Kill as many as possible," because it was your aim to kill as many people as possible. It's not true that you wanted to prevent this and protect this. And I heard you say over the radio, but I can't remember how far before the fall of Srebrenica it was, that you would take your revenge on the men of Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Sir, your Prosecutors will have to bring in that statement of mine if it exists.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. The Prosecution didn't hear that. I heard it. I listened to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: No speech, please. Just ask the questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says here under item 1: "Cease all operations ..." Item 2: "Stop the forces ... at the positions reached and prevent their entry into Srebrenica." Item 3, and the date is the 16th of April, 1993. After you arrived in Srebrenica and the Army of Republika Srpska had liberated the part inhabited by the Serbs, and that's how the Srebrenica protected zone was established. "Ensure the pacification of the town in such a way that the Muslim forces surrender their weapons to UNPROFOR ..." not the Serbs, UNPROFOR. And then UNPROFOR will store them on a two-key basis jointly with the Serb forces. Item 5: "After the surrender of weapons all the Muslim soldiers shall be treated like other civilians." "Provide protection for all civilians and give them the freedom to choose whether they want to stay or go." Item 6: "Do not conduct any investigations into war crimes until the situation around Srebrenica is settled." 7: "Carry the order out immediately and fully and inform me thereof." So the army stopped at the lines reached. It did not enter Srebrenica until 1995. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: No. No, that's not right. That's not how it was because you, sir, had the intention of cleansing Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: When you try to dupe the United Nations and behave towards the civilians as you did -- yes, you did. You killed the population and children, and there were lots of 14-year-old children buried last year. And people's eyes were full of tears, because to kill a 14-year-old child that's terrible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You're wasting my time.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: So are you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There was never a female body found or the body of a minor child under the age of 16 found during the exhumation. And now we can move on to page 153 -- 53.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: The Judges are here. The Prosecution is here. Your Defence is there. In Potocari the -- every buried person has a name and surname. So if I'm telling lies, I'll sit in your place and you'll sit in my place and testify against me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Everything can be checked out. It will only take you 24 hours. You can get a list of all the names buried.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Sir, please calm down. Mr. Karadzic, this -- as I told you several times, this is not a place for you to make a statement. You said there was never a female body found or the body of a minor child under the age of 16 found during the exhumation. You should put your statement to the witness, whether the witness agrees with it or not. Your statement does not help us at all. Sir, do you agree with that? Whether there was never a female body or the body of a minor child found during the exhumation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I've just told you. Everything is accessible to you in Potocari. You have the names and surnames written up on the slabs. The planes have started flying, so people can bring in the names of the people. I did not conduct the exhumations, whether there were women or not, but 66 women were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] OTP 65 ter 00053 next, please, and then that will be all for today. The OTP document 65 ter 00053. This is the transcript of a meeting of the popular Assembly of Republika Srpska, the 33rd session held on the 21st of July, 1993. And I'd like to draw your attention to the last -- it hasn't come up on our screens yet but the last sentence. Perhaps I can read it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: In the meantime, I take it that you do not object to the admission of the last document, his order.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And the number is?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, that will be Exhibit D43.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. This will be the last question, Mr. Karadzic, for today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll read it out. It's on page 02150376. 12031576 and 77. I think it's the same page in English. I'll read out what I said at the Assembly meeting. Once again not to be broadcast -- not for the media. It's not propaganda. If you take this with -- situation with Srebrenica, I think that it's a point to us, because if we had entered Srebrenica, people would have entered whose families had been killed. 1.200 Serbs were killed up until 1993. Up until the end, it was 3.500. So 1.200 Serbs were killed. There would have been blood up to our knees and we could have lost the country because of that. That is why I consider that Morillon saved us, not the Muslims, when he entered Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: You're right, sir, yes. Morillon did save you. You're quite right there. Morillon -- it was in front of Morillon's eyes that the shooting took place. I think there was a man from UNPROFOR who was wounded as well, and Morillon watched it all. Yes, that's right. Morillon was very good for you. And you mentioned Cutileiro, that Cutileiro of yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, do you accept that up until that point around Srebrenica, 1.200 Serbs were killed and who killed them, I ask you?

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: Do you know how many Muslims were killed?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That's not what I'm asking you now.

utterances.speaker: KDZ064
utterances.text: I don't know. I came to Srebrenica from another municipality. I have no idea what happened in Srebrenica, just as you don't know what happened in my village. But, of course, you know everything because you were the commander. You were the commander. You issued the orders. You were the number-one man.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We will adjourn for today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to request that the OTP 65 ter document 00053, pages 376 and 377, with the marked text that I read out, be tendered into evidence, please, as a Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that will be Exhibit D44.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, it must have been a long day for you. We will continue tomorrow. In the meantime, I would request to you not to discuss with anybody about your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, this is not tiring to me, because I want to show what kind of man he is that did all this, and now he pretends to be innocent. Well, why have you then, gentlemen, brought in an innocent man? Why have you brought in an innocent man here if he's innocent? It's not an effort to me. I can sit here for three days and nights if need be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. We will continue tomorrow, tomorrow afternoon, 2.15.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 22nd day of April, 2010, at 2.15 p.m.
